about.title: Lompoc Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Workers across Lompoc — from vineyard and flower-farm crews to contractors and aerospace-adjacent employers near Vandenberg — face daily physical risk. When an injury happens on the job, California's workers' compensation system is usually the only path against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. But that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate third-party claim worth pursuing alongside workers' comp. Lompoc's mix of agricultural, industrial, and municipal work sites means these overlapping claims come up often. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured workers with an independent attorney who can look at your situation, explain your options in plain terms, and help you understand whether a third-party claim applies to your case.

items.title: Understanding the Exclusive Remedy Rule
items.desc: California generally limits your claim against your employer to workers' compensation, no matter who was at fault. An independent attorney can help you understand what that rule does and doesn't cover in your specific situation.

items.title: Spotting Third-Party Liability
items.desc: If a negligent subcontractor, equipment maker, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, that party may fall outside the workers' comp system entirely. These third-party claims carry a two-year filing deadline, so timing matters.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an on-the-job injury. Reporting within 30 days protects your rights, and an attorney can help you understand what documentation to keep along the way.

items.question: I was hurt on a Lompoc job site — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is your only path against your employer directly, regardless of fault. But if someone outside your employer — like a subcontractor, equipment supplier, or another driver — contributed to the injury, you may also have a separate third-party claim. An independent attorney can review the facts and explain which paths apply.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer in Lompoc?
items.answer: California law generally requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate your claim, so it's best to report as soon as you're able. This applies whether the injury happened on a Lompoc farm, job site, or municipal facility.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No — retaliation against a worker for reporting an on-the-job injury is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation after an injury near Rt 1, H Street, or elsewhere in Lompoc, an independent attorney can help you understand your options.
